Did you know that you are not limited just by the size of your kiln when making large ceramics! The best way to build big pottery in my opinion his with coils. I’m making a floor lamp for a client and decided that stacking multiple pieces was how I was going to get the hight required for a piece of clay furniture! I love how that pottery really is just using the same dozen or so techniques in a bunch of different combinations, and that your creativity can allow you to really break through what is “possible”. This is only one piece in a huge series of lighting and showroom decor for the new Elliott Cole Home by Basecamp Design! I cannot wait to share more and show everything in the space soon. Here’s a completed apothecary jar and a full overview of how it’s made. For this type of lidded jar, the base and lid are thrown from one continuous piece of clay, then cut open and trimmed to create the inner edges and gallery so the lid doesn’t slide off. I like this type of piece because it has a continuous line from the base to the top of the knob. It’s a very elegant shape and one I imagine would look lovely on a shelf holding trinkets, spices, or chocolates. #pottery #studioceramics #wheelthrown #handmade #potteryartist

Throwing a Donut on the Wheel Center your clay and compress it into a wide, flat puck. Poke through the center down to the wheel head and slowly stretch it open to create the donut hole. Split the ring 50/50—leave a base slightly thicker than your future walls. Pull up the inner wall first, then the outer wall. Join the walls together. It doesn’t matter which one overlaps—adjust based on how the clay moves. Before joining, I thin out the edges to avoid a step at the seam. Important! Remove any slip and excess water from the seam—otherwise, it will crack during drying or firing. Once the walls are joined, the trapped air inside acts as a support structure, allowing you to refine the shape and compress the seam. Trim the excess clay inside and out, and your donut is ready! Follow me for more wheel-throwing tips! … … #ceramics #potteryvideos #pottery #fyp #usa
